title: No launch on a shortcut to a file extension even the default program is set (*.lnk)

status.label: Needs exact launch sequence
status.detail: Screenshots and a diagnostic ZIP are supplied, but wording alternates between .lnk shortcuts and custom .des/.dis files.

next_action.label: Clarify shortcut target and Run query
next_action.reason: The file/shortcut distinction and exact result selected determine which launch path is failing.

judgment.rationale: Screenshots show custom .des/.dis associations and the reporter supplied a diagnostic ZIP, but it is unclear whether PowerToys Run launches a .lnk, the .des/.dis target, or another search result. That distinction changes the path to investigate.
evidence: Report identifies PowerToys Run 0.85 and custom .des/.dis files associated with an application.
Reporter says those associations work outside PowerToys Run but nothing happens when launching through PowerToys Run.
Screenshots and an October 2024 diagnostic ZIP are attached; the maintainer request for a report was answered.
No linked fix PR found in the issue timeline or PR search.
judgment.recommended_action: Ask for the exact PowerToys Run query/result and whether it launches a .lnk shortcut or the .des/.dis target, plus current-version confirmation.

fix_assessment.rationale: A PowerToys Run shell-launch or file-association defect is plausible for custom file types, but the report does not identify whether the failing item is the shortcut or its target.

proposed_fixes.title: Preserve shell association resolution for custom shortcut targets
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Red hypothesis: the PowerToys Run launch path may resolve a shortcut or custom file target using a path-specific route that bypasses the registered Windows association for .des/.dis files.
plan: Confirm the exact query, selected result, and whether the selected item is a .lnk or the .des/.dis target.
Trace the confirmed item through PowerToys Run result resolution and shell association dispatch to identify where the target association is lost.
Preserve the resolved shell association on the affected path and add a regression test for a custom extension reached through a shortcut.
verification: On a current build, compare launching the target through Explorer with the exact Run query and selected result.
Verify the configured program launches and ordinary .lnk and extension launches still work.

confidence.rationale: Useful screenshots and diagnostics exist, but ambiguity between shortcut and target extension prevents identifying the launch branch.

issue_context.summary: A PowerToys Run user says launching an item associated with custom .des/.dis types does nothing, despite a Windows application association; screenshots and a diagnostic ZIP are attached.
known_information: Report lists PowerToys 0.85, WinGet installation, and PowerToys Run.
Named files are custom .des/.dis files under Start Menu folders; screenshots show their associations.
Reporter says the files work outside PowerToys Run and no action occurs when using PowerToys Run.
The reporter supplied a PowerToysReport ZIP after a maintainer asked for one.
inferences: The failure may involve custom extension association resolution or how PowerToys Run interprets a shortcut to a custom-extension target.
The text says both shortcut (*.lnk) and .des/.dis paths, so the exact selected item is ambiguous.
issue_context.analysis: Do not request existing screenshots or ZIP again. The missing discriminator is the precise query/result and whether the object is a .lnk or custom-extension target, which selects the shell-launch path to inspect.
initial_investigation: Read full issue, both comments, screenshot and diagnostic references, live labels, assignees, and updatedAt.
Confirmed reporter supplied the requested diagnostic ZIP.
Searched related PowerToys PRs by issue number; no linked fix found.

information_gaps.information: Exact PowerToys Run query and selected result, and whether the result is a .lnk shortcut or a .des/.dis target.
information_gaps.why_needed: Shortcut resolution and direct custom-extension dispatch are different paths; the report describes both.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Enter the exact query in PowerToys Run, identify the result selected, and say whether it opens the .lnk or .des/.dis target; give short numbered steps.

information_gaps.information: Whether this still reproduces on latest stable.
information_gaps.why_needed: The report is from version 0.85 and current behavior may have changed.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Check PowerToys About and include the installed version with the steps.

actions.label: Clarify shortcut target and Run query

comment.body:
Thanks for the screenshots showing custom .des/.dis associations and for the PowerToysReport attachment supplied after the maintainer asked. The report says shortcut (*.lnk) but also names .des/.dis files; it is unclear whether PowerToys Run launches the shortcut or the custom-extension target, which use different shell paths.
Please provide:
1. Whether this still occurs on the latest stable version.
2. If so, the exact PowerToys Run query, the result selected, and whether it is the .lnk or .des/.dis file; short numbered steps are sufficient.
This identifies the launch path without repeating evidence collection.

actions.label: Design fix
actions.note: Approve an evidence-gated fork-side investigation after confirming whether the shortcut or custom-extension target fails. This does not write upstream.
